description:
The only ORM and data access framework for Azure Table Storage in the .NET ecosystem.
ASCDataAccessLibrary gives .NET developers (6 through 10) an Entity-Framework-style experience — lambda expression queries, strongly-typed entities, automatic serialization, batch operations, and fluent extension methods — on top of the most cost-effective NoSQL cloud database available.

v4.5 adds adaptive local-memory governance to the DAL's single unified result cache: bounded query admission, O(1) table invalidation generations under the default write policy, expiry/cold-value maintenance, and machine/container memory-pressure awareness. Buffered reads use the shared cache by default; [CachePolicy] tunes TTL, append-only refresh, and invalidation without creating a second cache layer or relying on Redis/Table Storage.

Write idiomatic C# against Azure Table Storage and Azure Blob Storage without touching the raw SDK:
  • var customer = await new Customer().LoadAsync(x => x.CompanyId == id)
  • await customer.SaveAsync()
  • await customers.DeleteAsync()
  • [CachePolicy("5m")] on the entity → tune process-wide caching with write-through invalidation
  • await foreach (var row in da.StreamCollectionAsync(predicate)) → progressive-render UIs

Key features:
  • Lambda expression queries with automatic hybrid server-side / client-side OData splitting
  • Strongly-typed entities with transparent decimal precision, large string chunking, and enum serialization
  • Dynamic entities (DynamicEntity) for schema-free, runtime-defined data — telemetry, ETL, multi-tenant config
  • Batch insert / update / delete up to any size — auto-chunked at Azure's 100-entity limit
  • Cursor-based pagination with continuation tokens
  • IAsyncEnumerable streaming for Azure Tables — StreamCollectionAsync yields rows as the SDK pages them
  • Adaptive local result caching — bounded buffered reads use a 120-second default TTL; [CachePolicy] tunes behavior
  • Row-completion events — DataAccess<T>.RowCompleted reports committed single-row and batch work
  • SingleFlight coalescing — concurrent identical cache misses share one Azure round-trip
  • Azure Blob Storage with IAsyncEnumerable streaming, lambda tag filtering, and FFmpeg video compression
  • Persistent resumable work queues (QueueData<T> + StateList<T>) with crash recovery and position tracking
  • Azure Table Storage session management for ASP.NET Core, desktop, console, and background service apps
  • First-class ILogger provider — standard .NET structured logging backed by Azure Table Storage
  • TableStorage.Configure() once in Program.cs — credentials resolved automatically across the entire app

Built and maintained by Answer Sales Calls Inc. (ASC). Targets Azure.Data.Tables SDK v12 (no legacy Cosmos.Table dependency). Ships as net9.0 and is compatible with .NET 9 and .NET 10 SDK builds.

## Release Notes — ASCDataAccessLibrary v4.5.0

### Release summary

v4.5 makes long-running Azure Table applications more predictable under traffic and memory
pressure without changing data ownership, ordinary DAL call sites, or requiring a schema migration.

### What this means for an app

- **Predictable local memory:** cache pressure only evicts a local optimization; the next caller
  performs its normal authoritative Azure Table read. The DAL neither writes cached values back to
  storage, requires Redis, nor forces GC.
- **Fresh post-write reads without cache-wide scans:** under the default `InvalidateOnWrite = true`
  policy, a table generation immediately rejects stale same-process results in O(1), then bounded
  maintenance releases their retained memory. An explicit opt-out retains its documented TTL behavior.
- **One bounded owner for disposable projections:** `DeviceCache<TKey,TValue>` is suitable for
  small process-local display/access projections, not sessions, jobs, large Blob/PDF bytes, or
  cross-instance state.
- **Safer hosted lifecycles without a startup migration:** ordinary hosts keep their existing
  automatic session maintenance. `UseExternalMaintenance` is an optional integration for a host
  that already owns one scheduler; failed session persistence is never reported as committed.
- **Clear coordination semantics:** conditional write APIs expose Azure 409/412 outcomes, leaving
  business retry and reconciliation with the caller rather than replaying a stale action.
- **Indexed alias queries with existing syntax:** a simple `PartitionKey` / `RowKey` property
  alias keeps the caller's query expression while the DAL targets Azure's indexed key column.

### What changed

- Added adaptive device/server cache governance to `DataAccessCache`. The DAL now admits only
  bounded buffered query collections, tracks conservative entry weights, expires entries through
  a bounded maintenance pass, and sheds sampled cold values when the process budget or CLR
  machine/container memory pressure requires it. Cache pressure never writes to Azure Table
  Storage, never requires Redis, never forces GC, and never changes the success of CRUD reads.
- Replaced O(n) write-side table-cache scans with table invalidation generations. Under the default
  `InvalidateOnWrite = true` policy, a DAL write marks that table stale in O(1); stale values are
  rejected immediately on their next read and physically released by the shared maintenance pass.
- Added `DeviceCache<TKey,TValue>`, `CreateDeviceCache`, `Configure`, `Maintain`, and
  `GetDiagnostics` so application transient caches can share this one bounded in-process store
  instead of creating untracked static dictionaries.
- Corrected conservative cache accounting for empty and small results; maintenance now reaches
  expired entries beyond fresh prefixes while retaining only bounded removal batches. The DAL's
  shadow-partition dedupe hints now use the bounded account-qualified device cache and exclude
  primary-key aliases, preventing unbounded retention of unique values such as log IDs.

- Added `DataAccess<T>.RowCompleted`, a simple delegate event raised after a successful
  single-row write/delete or committed batch transaction. It supplies the storage account,
  table name, operation, and existing affected entity objects so consumers can perform their
  own follow-up work without a lookup. Subscriber failures do not make a committed DAL write
  appear to fail.
- Documented the automatic `AppTableList` registry (`ShadowTable`): a best-effort, derived
  inventory of table names the DAL has touched. It is not a schema, security, or migration API.
- Documented the DateTime write boundary: valid dates use UTC semantics; pre-1601
  `DateTime` / `DateTimeOffset` values are omitted so Azure Table Storage does not reject the
  row. The guide now explains the different merge and replace consequences.
- Documented `FromConnString(defaultMaxFileSizeBytes)` for private, configuration-driven Blob
  clients and its required `AccountName`, `AccountKey`, and `ContainerName` values.
- Corrected `ApplicationLogEntry` storage guidance: `Category` is the Azure Table
  `PartitionKey`; it is not a monthly timestamp bucket.
- Corrected shadow-catalog maintenance guidance: preserve application/log/audit source data;
  rebuild or clean only derived `AppShadowPartitions` data when necessary.
- Added opt-in conditional single-row writes: `TableWriteCondition`,
  `ManageDataConditionallyAsync`, and `GetFreshRowAsync` let cooperating writers use Azure
  insert/ETag preconditions without changing existing unconditional writes.
- Added automatic alias-to-key query rewriting so simple `PartitionKey` / `RowKey` aliases use
  indexed Azure query columns without changing existing query call sites.
- Hardened session and logging lifecycles: clean idle managed sessions can release strong
  ownership, dirty sessions are not falsely marked committed after a failed write, same-ID
  creation/expiry is fenced, external host maintenance is opt-in, and log flush ticks coalesce
  with a final shutdown drain.

### Cache model clarification

`DataAccessCache` is the only DAL result cache. Buffered reads participate by default;
undecorated entity types use the 120-second default TTL. `[CachePolicy]` tunes TTL,
append-only refresh, and write invalidation. The obsolete `DataAccessRequestCache` / AsyncLocal
memoization API is not part of v4.5. The normal cache target flexes to five percent of runtime/
container memory, bounded by an 8 MB minimum and 256 MB safety ceiling; entries remain capped at
512 KB and buffered collections at 250 items. Applications normally need no cache configuration.
Applications may optionally schedule bounded maintenance through their existing
background-work mechanism.

### Compatibility and upgrade notes

Existing ordinary CRUD, query, batch, Blob, queue, session, and logging calls remain compatible.
No application data-table deletion or required startup change is needed for this release. Existing applications that used
the obsolete beta request-cache API should migrate to `DataAccessCache`; see section 26 of the
packaged getting-started guide. Read `getting-started-guide-44.md` before enabling a
RowCompleted subscriber or cleaning a derived shadow catalog.
